editorial.tldr: Three reinforcement-learning items landed over two weeks: an InfoQ talk on OpenAI's Agent RFT fine-tuning platform, and two arXiv papers applying RL to fraud detection and federated microgrid coordination. The items share a topic, not a storyline — each is a standalone read, not a developing event.
editorial.whats_new: The latest addition is an arXiv paper proposing constraint-aware aggregation for federated RL, replacing standard FedAvg so microgrid energy-coordination agents respect system-level constraints instead of just averaging local updates.
editorial.why_it_matters: For platform engineers running RL fine-tuning, the InfoQ talk is the practical read on OpenAI's managed Agent RFT platform; the two arXiv papers are narrower academic results (fraud detection, energy-grid coordination) with no direct deployment path.
editorial.take_for_builders: Evaluating OpenAI's managed Agent RFT platform for reasoning-model fine-tuning? Treat the two arXiv papers (fraud-detection Pareto-DQN, federated microgrid RL) as domain-specific research ideas, not production-ready recipes for your own RL training pipeline.
